finding.title: Delete or wire up tool/curate_curricula/sefaria_settings.py — a vestigial placeholder never referenced by the documented workflow

evidence.quote: # (placeholder — actual settings live in Sefaria-Project's sefaria/local_settings.py)

finding.why: The file documents its own invocation via a PYTHONPATH trick that nothing else in the repo uses; README.md's actual Setup section instead has the developer hand-write a real sefaria/local_settings.py inside the external Sefaria-Project checkout. Repo-wide grep for 'sefaria_settings' finds zero importers or references. Even if it were picked up, its body is only a comment, so it does nothing — it's dead weight with instructions that contradict the real workflow.

finding.title: Fix stale password_hasher.dart path printed by tool/argon2id_benchmark.dart — file moved from features/auth to features/account
finding.why: The benchmark tool prints instructions telling whoever runs it to 'Update Argon2idParams.production in lib/features/auth/domain/services/password_hasher.dart', but Argon2idParams and PasswordHasher actually live under lib/features/account/ — the feature was evidently renamed/relocated after this script was written and the printed path was never updated. Anyone following the tool's own output would open a path that doesn't exist.
finding.recommendation: Update the stdout.writeln call to print lib/features/account/domain/services/password_hasher.dart.
acceptance_criteria: argon2id_benchmark.dart's printed path matches the real location of Argon2idParams.production

finding.title: Define a retention policy for completed-round device-test workflow.js scripts instead of letting run2/run3 accumulate in tool/ indefinitely
finding.why: Each script hardcodes one specific device IP, throwaway test-account PINs, and references specific numbered fixes ('FIX#7', 'FIX#9') from one already-completed testing round (run2, run3). git history shows later rounds (run-6, run-7, per the repo's recent commit log) left no equivalent *.workflow.js files behind, so retention is inconsistent — a reader can't tell whether run2/run3 are kept deliberately as re-runnable regression scripts or are simply uncleaned leftovers, and there is no tool/README documenting either answer.
finding.recommendation: Document a retention rule for run-N workflow scripts (e.g. archive completed rounds under docs/audits/ next to the bug-log report they produced, or delete once their fixes have landed and been verified), and apply it to run2/run3.
acceptance_criteria: tool/ (or a new tool/README) states the retention rule for *.workflow.js device-test scripts
run2/run3 scripts are archived, removed, or explicitly kept per that stated rule

finding.title: Delete or archive the dead Story-15.13 content-upload pipeline (tool/seed_content.dart, tool/seed_text_content.dart, tool/upload_to_firebase.{js,sh})
finding.why: None of these 4 files appear anywhere in the Makefile (grep confirms only seed_content_db.dart and validate_seed_coverage.dart are wired in); docs/linear-status.md:167 shows the feature they serve, 'DNI-121 | 15.13: Cloud Content Storage & Multilingual Fetch', as Canceled; and the in-app consumer of the Firebase Storage path they write to (CloudContentServiceProvider in lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/providers/cloud_content_providers.dart) has zero callers outside its own generated .g.dart file. The bucket name they target ('torah-study-tracker.firebasestorage.app') matches the real production bucket in lib/firebase_options.dart:53, so anyone who trusts the still-present usage comments and re-runs this chain writes real, unused data into the production Storage bucket that ST-1 already flags as having no committed security rules. upload_to_firebase.js and upload_to_firebase.sh have also already drifted from each other while unmaintained: the .sh version supports --dry-run/--curriculum=X, the .js version has no argument parsing at all and always uploads everything for real.
finding.recommendation: Delete tool/seed_content.dart, tool/seed_text_content.dart, tool/upload_to_firebase.js, tool/upload_to_firebase.sh (or move them to a tool/_archive/ with a header banner citing DNI-121/Canceled if the team wants to keep them as reference). Update docs/explainers/content-database.md's 'Where the code lives' list and docs/api-contracts.md:92, which both still cite these files as active pipeline components.
acceptance_criteria: tool/seed_content.dart, tool/seed_text_content.dart, tool/upload_to_firebase.js, tool/upload_to_firebase.sh no longer exist at HEAD, or each carries a header stating they are retired (Story DNI-121, Canceled) and naming any current replacement
docs/explainers/content-database.md and docs/api-contracts.md:92 no longer list these files as active build-pipeline components
grep -rL 'DNI-121\|retired' over any files kept returns empty

finding.title: Mark tool/text_extract/ as retired in-repo and fix extract_books.py's footnote-stripping regression before any reuse
finding.why: docs/seed-build.md:6,123 explicitly states the daily-content resolvers were 'ported from the retired tool/text_extract/main.py', and the live pipeline (make seed → tool/seed/build_text_cache.dart, tool/seed/build_daily_content.dart) never invokes anything under tool/text_extract/. Yet the directory's own README still reads as a live runbook (present-tense 'Builds…', full venv setup, a 'Failure modes' section) with no pointer to the replacement or the fact it's retired. Worse, extract_books.py's _clean() (which shares the exact same directory/README/venv and produces tool/data/curriculum_books.json — the very file build_text_cache.dart now treats as a static committed input) only strips HTML *tags* via a bare `<[^>]+>` regex; it does not remove footnote *bodies* the way its own sibling main.py's `_FOOTNOTE` regex does, or the way the runtime's HebrewUtils.cleanSefariaText does (documented as the 'BUG-5' fix in sefaria_mongo.dart:19 and seed_content_db.dart:583-591). A contributor trusting the README who re-runs extract_books.py to add a book would regenerate curriculum_books.json/book_text_cache.json with Sefaria footnote text merged back into the main body — reintroducing exactly the corruption the rest of the codebase guards against three times over.
finding.recommendation: Add a retirement banner to tool/text_extract/README.md pointing at tool/seed/build_text_cache.dart and build_daily_content.dart as the current replacement. If the directory is kept for reference/history rather than deleted, fix extract_books.py's _clean() to strip footnote bodies the same way main.py's _FOOTNOTE regex does, so it can't silently corrupt data if someone runs it anyway.
acceptance_criteria: tool/text_extract/README.md states the retirement and names the current replacement tools, or the directory is removed entirely
A test asserts extract_books.py's _clean() removes an `…` span wholesale (matching main.py's _FOOTNOTE behavior) — red before the fix, green after, or the file is deleted
